title: Regret Price of Unknown Rare-Treatment Intensities in Audited Capacity-Constrained Policy Choice

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery produced a fully discharged TeX note with two-way finite-sample to marked-Poisson transfer, disclosed-intensity thinning, rational decision programs, and a positive price at one calibrated point. The math panel passed, but the general referee graded the package incremental because the phase frontier remains open and the numerical certificate lacks an executable ledger. The fixed field floor was not met; a regional phase theorem would require a new research result.
tldr: When treatment labels and treated cases are both rare, the labels recovered by an audit converge to four marked-Poisson counts. In a two-stratum capacity problem with fixed observed outcome margins, the minimax welfare regret over \(\Pi_n\) when the two rare-treatment intensities are unknown is strictly larger than the regret over \(\Pi_n^K\) when they are disclosed, even though the nuisance box and one-stratum capacity action semantics are identical. Parameter-free kernels transfer arbitrary randomized policies in both directions, exact rational certificates place the price above \(0.000608\) at unit effective intensity, and a deterministic arbitrary-tolerance program at rational \(c\) and \(d\) yields auditable brackets and attaining original-data rules at the headline input. The strict effect persists on an explicit neighborhood but disappears at important boundaries, leaving the exact zero-to-positive phase frontier as the open problem.
gap: Missing-treatment policy inference is developed under fixed laws, regular treatment-choice theory uses Gaussian limit experiments, and numerical minimax work supplies convergent finite games. None of these results compares unknown and disclosed rare-treatment intensities when only finitely many audited treated outcomes survive asymptotically.
fill: The project proves a uniform two-way full-record comparison to a marked-Poisson game, exact oracle thinning, a terminating rational certification theorem for rational limit-game inputs with original-record attainment at the headline input, and a strict all-policy information price with an explicit robust neighborhood.
